## Lisbon 5-Day Trip Plan: Museums, Walks, and Seafood

A comfortable, culture-first itinerary for one adult traveler with a **EUR 1,100** on-the-ground budget excluding flights. I’ve paced it for easy walking, 1–2 major sights per day, and built in a rainy-day backup.

## Day-by-Day Lisbon Itinerary and Budget

| Day | Focus | Plan | Est. Cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| Apr 12 | Historic center | Baixa + Chiado walking loop; Carmo area; sunset at Miradouro de São Pedro de Alcântara; seafood dinner | **EUR 165** |
| Apr 13 | Museums + riverside | Museu Nacional do Azulejo; Alfama stroll; Lisbon Cathedral area; casual seafood lunch; evening river walk | **EUR 175** |
| Apr 14 | Belém day | Jerónimos exterior and Belém district walk; MAAT or Museu dos Coches; pastéis stop; grilled fish dinner | **EUR 190** |
| Apr 15 | Neighborhoods + viewpoints | Tram-free walking day through Bairro Alto, Príncipe Real, and Estrela; market lunch; relaxed dinner | **EUR 180** |
| Apr 16 | Final culture day | Choose one major museum or gallery; last shopping/walks; farewell seafood lunch before departure | **EUR 140** |

## 5-Day Itinerary with Realistic Pace

### Day 1: Arrival + Baixa and Chiado
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
- Morning: Arrive, check in, and keep the first hours light with a coffee stop and easy walk through Baixa.
- Afternoon: Walk up through Chiado, browse small shops, and visit the Carmo area if energy is good.
- Dinner: Start with **grilled sardines, octopus salad, or arroz de marisco** in a relaxed neighborhood restaurant.
- Pace: Easy; aim for 6–8 km of walking max.

### Day 2: Azulejos, Alfama, and Old Lisbon
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- Morning: Visit **Museu Nacional do Azulejo** for a strong cultural start.
- Afternoon: Wander Alfama slowly, stopping at viewpoints and the cathedral area.
- Dinner: Choose a tascas-style seafood place for **bacalhau, clams, or shellfish rice**.
- Pace: Moderate; expect hills and cobblestones.

### Day 3: Belém Culture Day
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/map.svg
- Morning: Head to Belém early to avoid crowds and walk the riverfront.
- Afternoon: Visit **MAAT** or **Museu dos Coches** depending on your interest; add a pastry stop at Pastéis de Belém.
- Dinner: Book a seafood dinner back in the center or along the river.
- Pace: Moderate; use tram or taxi for the Belém transfer to save time and energy.

### Day 4: Bairro Alto, Príncipe Real, and Estrela
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/wind.svg
- Morning: Start in Príncipe Real for calm streets, gardens, and design shops.
- Afternoon: Continue to Bairro Alto and Estrela for a scenic walking circuit and viewpoint breaks.
- Dinner: Go for a slightly nicer seafood meal tonight if you want one splurge.
- Pace: Relaxed; this is your best day for wandering without a strict schedule.

### Day 5: Final Museum + Departure Buffer
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/calendar.svg
- Morning: Pick one final museum or gallery near your hotel to keep the day low-stress.
- Afternoon: Do last-minute shopping, coffee, and a short final walk.
- Dinner: If you depart later, fit in one last seafood lunch rather than a long dinner.
- Pace: Very light; leave space for transit and packing.

## Rainy-Day Backup Plan

### Indoor Lisbon Plan
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/cloud-rain.svg
- Swap any walking-heavy day for **Museu Nacional do Azulejo**, **MAAT**, **Museu dos Coches**, or a longer café-and-market day.
- Add **Time Out Market** for an easy food-focused fallback with seafood options.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/8/83/Lobster%2C_Time_Out_Market_Lisboa_%2850661858143%29.jpg Alt=Add **Time Out Market** for an easy food-focused fallback with seafood options, Lisbon, Portugal
- Use trams, metro, or taxis to reduce wet-weather walking and hills.

## Budget Fit for EUR 1,100

- Accommodation: **EUR 500–650** for 4 nights in a well-located mid-range stay
- Food and drinks: **EUR 220–300**
- Local transport: **EUR 40–70**
- Museums and entries: **EUR 70–120**
- Buffer/souvenirs: **EUR 60–120**

This keeps you comfortably within budget while allowing one nicer seafood dinner and a few paid museum visits.
